text.p: - Slovenia's Constitutional Court is expected to decide on Tuesday whether electoral referendums should take place before of after general elections set for November 10. However, the referendum outcome would not apply to the November elections.
- Experts claim the lenght of training courses for officers in Slovenian army is too short. The Defence Ministry said the minimum lenght was one year.
- Slovenian electicity companies ask government to raise electricity prices, which are about 29 percent below the European Union average.
- The city of Ribnica has the higest unemployment rate in Slovenia with about 30 percent, well above the country's average of 13.3 percent.
- Experts are as yet unable to tell for how long a border tunnel between Slovenia and Austria, whose ceiling crushed on Friday, would be closed for renovation.

- The government is expected to increase control over prices prior to the November elections in order to keep the monthly inflation rate at last month's level. August monthly inflation was 0.1 percent.
- Several people said they were healed from various ailments during a three-day visit of priest Emilie Tardiff from the Dominican Republic in Ljubljana.
